releases.notes:
- Lists open at the top while they load and sort; floating arrows (and ZL / ZR on a New 3DS) jump to the start or the end.
- Your own themes: Settings -> Edit the theme changes every colour with a finger and shows it at once on both screens, from any theme or a blank template; the web page has the same editor. They are kept as files in /nsa/themes/.
- HOME theme: icon grids in pages that turn sideways (tap a dot, or drag the bar, to jump to one), and sheets close when pulled down.
- Pixel theme: the digits, B and Z are drawn by hand, so 5 and S, 8 and B no longer look alike.
- New guide chapter: Your own themes.

- A .3dsx can be installed in the HOME Menu (SD card, the .3dsx's actions, "Install in the HOME Menu"): it becomes a real title, not a forwarder, so it starts and quits like any other and the .3dsx is no longer needed.
- Its icon and name come from the .3dsx; the banner is drawn from them, or made from a picture of yours.
- Installing the same .3dsx again updates the title; a newer .3dsx needs to be installed again to update it.

- System is now three groups: Information (console, network, storage, battery), Console settings (Date and time, Wi-Fi connections) and Hardware tests.
- Buttons and touch: every key, the Circle Pad, the C-Stick, the touch screen and the 3D and volume sliders, live, with a counter of what is left to try and a magnified view of each stick's centre to spot drift.
- Motion sensors: the accelerometer and the gyroscope live, and a recording of both to a CSV file in /nsa/logs that keeps going with the lid closed.
- Guide: a chapter for the hardware tests, and the Wi-Fi and Date and time tours go through Console settings.

- Web interface PIN (Settings -> Web PIN): a new random one at each start (as before), a fixed one you type on a numeric keypad or make random, or none. When a browser asks for the PIN, the console shows it at the bottom of the screen.
- Remote install: two small buttons beside History turn the FTP server and the web server on or off, and show their address (the web one also its PIN and a QR code). History shows the last file's name.
- NSA's own boot logo when it starts from the HOME menu (the installed CIA), with a day and a night look.
- Titles: "Extract ExeFS" copies a title's code, icon, banner and logo to the SD card.
- FTP: Dolphin and other file managers that open several connections browse without hanging (5 sessions, a single file in a listing, a longer wait for data connections).
- Guide: new steps for all this, and the Wi-Fi tour no longer gets stuck when A is pressed on another row.

- Taps near a list's right end press the row or button again: the scrollbar is grabbed only in the narrow gap beside it.
- The web page no longer hangs when a browser forces https:// on its port (HTTPS is not supported): that connection is closed at once so the browser falls back to http://, and a silent connection is dropped after 4 seconds instead of 30.
- FTP: when all 3 places are taken by connections left idle (a file manager such as Dolphin opens several), the one idle longest makes room for the new connection instead of answering "too many connections" until NSA restarts.

- Date and time (System -> Console): 12 or 24 hours and day or month first, the clock set from the Internet with your time zone and summer time, or picked on a calendar and time wheels.
- Installing a game that is already there keeps its save; an older version asks first and puts the save back. A saved download that was cut goes on where it stopped.
- Files extracts .zip and .7z archives, and the notification light blinks when a download, an install or a transfer ends.
- The web page is 30-60% faster, uploads reserve the file's size first, and extra data is found by the ID the game itself names.
- Fixes: System -> Network's gateway and DNS, the SD card's maker and date, copying a folder into itself, and pictures (a GIF) that closed the viewer.
- The guide shows only what is new in a chapter you have seen, marked New.

- Remote install no longer freezes NSA when something that is not a sender connects to port 5000 (an FTP client such as FileZilla pointed at the wrong port): after 5 seconds without data it shows an error and goes back to waiting. FTP is on port 5021.

- Wi-Fi connections: System -> Network keeps copies of the console's three connections (with an alias), writes them back, edits or deletes a connection, and connects at once when the console is offline.
- Advanced -> Dump NAND copies the system memory to the SD card faster, stopping at its last partition.
- Every progress bar shows the time left, and B asks before stopping a copy, install or download (what was half written is deleted).
- FTP resumes cut transfers (REST), and the FTP and web servers wait for the Wi-Fi and come back with it.
- Store: Vapecord plugins, ndsForwarder and YANBF install, and apps that are neither a CIA nor a 3DSX show when they are installed.

- The guide now offers what is new in 0.9: selecting several files, music in the background, game mods, your own stores, and the transfer progress and QR code of From your computer.
- The music chapter explains repeat and how to get back to the song that plays.

- Store: add your own stores (.unistore) by QR code or link, see every entry a store offers, and install right after opening it (it no longer waits for the console's apps to be checked); zips unpack much faster.
- Files: select several items to copy, move, install or delete at once; big folders are deleted faster.
- Game mods: Cleanup lists the LayeredFS mods in /luma/titles and whether their game is installed, and deleting a game offers to delete its mods too.
- Music: the player keeps playing in the background after B, jumps instantly within an MP3 and can repeat the list or one track.
- FTP: FileZilla no longer waits 20 s before each transfer; transfers over FTP and the web page show their progress on the console, and the web page's address shows as a QR code.
- Every list sorts both ways, filters are icons, every grid has a tile size, and downloads start sooner on an Old 3DS.
